# Shale's surface, generated by tools/surface.shale from the source: never edit it by hand.
#
# Every part of the language a script or a user can observe, read from the
# Zig source and the preludes. The C port matches it byte for byte.
#
# Texts are as the source writes them, Zig's escapes kept (\" \\ \n).
# The variable parts are marked: {s} {d} {t} {c} {any} (Zig's format, its
# {{ and }} shown as one brace), {comptime} for a part Zig joins at compile
# time, {expr} for a Shale expression a prelude's `fail` joins in.
# A section the source can't give mechanically is at the end, marked BY HAND.

## Lua's names, refused by name (24): the name, its message
  string       the standard library is not in this language: call the builtin, `upper(s)`, not `string.upper(s)`
  table        the standard library is not in this language: call the builtin, `push(l, x)`, not `table.insert(l, x)`
  math         the standard library is not in this language
  os           the standard library is not in this language: `now()` is the only time
  io           the standard library is not in this language: `read`, `print`
  utf8         the standard library is not in this language
  coroutine    coroutines are not in this language
  debug        the standard library is not in this language
  package      the standard library is not in this language
  require      `require` is not in this language
  pcall        `pcall` is not in this language: `attempt(f, ...)` calls a function and gives its error as a value
  xpcall       `xpcall` is not in this language: `attempt(f, ...)` calls a function and gives its error as a value
  error        `error` is not in this language: `fail(msg)` stops the run with your message, and `attempt` catches it
  pairs        `pairs` is not in this language: `for k in keys(m) do ... m[k] ... end`
  ipairs       `ipairs` is not in this language: `for x in list do ... end`, or `for i = 1, #list do`
  setmetatable metatables are not in this language
  getmetatable metatables are not in this language
  type         `type` is not in this language
  select       varargs are not in this language
  unpack       multiple values are not in this language
  load         `load` is not in this language
  dofile       `dofile` is not in this language
  rawget       metatables are not in this language
  rawset       metatables are not in this language

### interp (26)
  argument   a `for` with a step of 0 never ends
  arithmetic `%` by zero
  arithmetic integer division by zero
  arithmetic negating {d} overflows 64 bits
  arithmetic {d} {s} {d} overflows 64 bits

  index      index {d} is outside the list (length {d}): only index {d} appends, and `push(l, x)` says so
  index      no key \"{s}\" in the map (`has_key` asks first)
  type       `#` of a map: use `count(m)`

  type       `==` on a list or a map is not in this language
  type       `for x in` a map: walk `keys(m)` instead
  type       `for x in` takes a list, given {s}
  type       `{s}` compares {s} with {s}
  type       `{s}` takes integers, and its left is {s}{s}
  type       `{s}` takes integers, and its right is {s}{s}
  type       a key must be an integer (a list) or a string (a map), not {s}
  type       a list cannot hold nil
  type       a list's keys are integers: this one is a list, indexed by a string

## The budgets (16): name, the core's default, the CLI's, whether `--budget` sets it, what it counts
  steps          5000000    5000000    --budget Statements, expressions and charged work, in steps.
  arena_bytes    16777216   16777216   --budget Bytes of the values' arena.
  call_depth     64         64         --budget Calls of script functions in progress at once.
  programs       1000       1000       --budget Programs a run may start on Linux, by `run` and `job_start` (metal starts none).
  output_bytes   262144     65536      --budget Bytes printed.
  reads          10000      10000      --budget Store reads, by count.
  read_bytes     67108864   67108864   --budget Bytes read from the store.
  changes        1000       1000       --budget Store changes, by count.
  change_bytes   16777216   16777216   --budget Bytes written to the store.
  source_bytes   65536      65536      no       Bytes of source.
  nesting        200        200        no       How deeply the source may nest.
  depth          2000       2000       no       Expressions and statements the walk is inside of at once, across every call.
  kept_bytes     1048576    1048576    --budget Bytes of the values the VM still reaches, copied into a fresh arena at each `yield`.
  machine_bytes  16777216   16777216   --budget One arena, beside the values', for the parse's tree, the compiled code, the frames' slots, the operand stack, the `..` chains' parts and a yield's copying.
  call_bytes     1048576    67108864   --budget The most bytes one `read` (or one scan) takes from the store in one call.
  call_entries   256        256        --budget The entries one `walk` call takes from its folders' listings, each a stat if it is kept.
  const default_output_bytes = 262144
  const default_source_bytes = 65536
  const kept_bytes_most = 268435456
  const machine_bytes_most = 1073741824
  the names `--budget` and a `-- budget:` line take: steps reads read_bytes output_bytes changes change_bytes arena_bytes call_bytes call_entries kept_bytes machine_bytes call_depth programs

## The budgets a stop names (15), `budget <name>`, each with its message (a second text is what it says when its own text could not be made)
  steps         the step budget ({d} steps) ran out  ||  the step budget ran out
  arena         the arena budget ran out
  call_depth    calls nest deeper than the call-depth budget ({d})  ||  calls nest deeper than the call-depth budget
  output        the output budget ran out
  reads         the store-read budget (count) ran out
  read_bytes    the store-read budget (bytes) ran out
  changes       the store-change budget (count) ran out
  change_bytes  the store-change budget (bytes) ran out
  source        the source is larger than the source budget
  nesting       the source nests deeper than the nesting budget
  depth         calls and the expressions inside them nest deeper than the depth budget
  kept          what the run keeps at a `yield` is past the kept budget ({d} bytes): raise it with `--budget kept_bytes=N` or the script's `-- budget: kept_bytes=N` line, up to {d}  ||  what the run keeps at a `yield` is past the kept budget
  machine       the machine's memory (the code, the frames, the operands) is past its budget ({d} bytes): raise it with `--budget machine_bytes=N` or the script's `-- budget: machine_bytes=N` line, up to {d}  ||  the machine's memory is past its budget
  programs      {d} programs a run, the `programs` budget: raise it with `--budget programs=N` or the script's `-- budget: programs=N` line  ||  the run's programs are past their budget
  cpu           a program's CPU time is past its budget

## The stop's report, as the CLI writes it (cli.zig printReport)
  pub fn printReport(r: *const script.Result, name: []const u8, preludes: []const parse_mod.Prelude, how: How, w: *std.Io.Writer) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
      if (how.verbose) {
          try w.print("── effects ({d}) ──\n", .{r.effects.len});
          for (r.effects) |e| try w.print("{s} {s}: {s}\n", .{ e.op, e.path, e.outcome });
      }
      if (how.verbose and how.records.len > 0) {
          try w.writeAll("── ran ──\n");
          for (how.records) |line| try w.print("{s}\n", .{line});
      }
      if (r.stop) |s| {
          try w.print("── stopped at {s}:{d}:{d}{s}{s}{s}: {s}{s}{s}: {s} ({d} steps)\n", .{ placeOf(s.function, name, preludes), s.line, s.column, if (s.function.len > 0) " (in `" else "", s.function, if (s.function.len > 0) "`)" else "", @tagName(s.class), if (s.budget != null) " " else "", if (s.budget) |b| @tagName(b) else "", s.message, r.steps });
          var k = s.trail.len;
          while (k > 0) {
              k -= 1;
              const c = s.trail[k];
              try w.print("   called from {s}:{d}:{d}{s}{s}{s}\n", .{ placeOf(c.function, name, preludes), c.line, c.column, if (c.function.len > 0) " (in `" else "", c.function, if (c.function.len > 0) "`)" else "" });
          }
      } else if (how.verbose) try w.print("── finished ({d} steps)\n", .{r.steps});
      const b = how.budgets;
      if (how.verbose or r.stop != null or pastHalf(.{ .steps = r.steps, .reads = r.reads, .read_bytes = r.read_bytes, .output = r.output.len }, b))
          try w.print("── used: {d} of {d} steps, {d} of {d} reads, {d} of {d} read bytes, {d} of {d} output bytes\n", .{ r.steps, b.steps, r.reads, b.reads, r.read_bytes, b.read_bytes, r.output.len, b.output_bytes });
  }
## The past-half rule (cli.zig pastHalf)
  pub fn pastHalf(u: Used, b: interp.Budgets) bool {
      return u.steps * 2 > b.steps or u.reads * 2 > b.reads or u.read_bytes * 2 > b.read_bytes or u.output * 2 > b.output_bytes;
  }
## The header's budgets line (cli.zig printHeaderBudgets)
  pub fn printHeaderBudgets(c: Command, w: *std.Io.Writer) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
      var first = true;
      inline for (settable, 0..) |field, k| {
          if (c.from_header[k]) {
              try w.print("{s}{s}={d}", .{ if (first) "── budgets from the script's header: " else ", ", field, @field(c.budgets, field) });
              first = false;
          }
      }
      if (!first) try w.writeAll("\n");
  }

## The CLI's usage (cli.zig usage)
  usage: shale [--root DIR] [--verbose] [--undo-on-stop] [--check] [--budget NAME=N]... [FILE [--args-stdin] | -e SOURCE] [NAME=VALUE]...
    --root DIR        the folder the script's paths are relative to (SHALE_ROOT, or here)
    --check           parse and compile the script, with its preludes, and run nothing
    --verbose         the effects, the programs run and what the run used, always
    --undo-on-stop    a run that stops puts back every path it changed (not a program's)
    --args-stdin      the FILE's NAME=VALUEs on stdin, one a line, each value raw to its end
    --budget NAME=N   one budget: steps, reads, read_bytes, output_bytes, changes,
                      change_bytes, arena_bytes, call_bytes, call_entries, programs,
                      kept_bytes (at most 256 MiB), machine_bytes (at most 1 GiB); a
                      script's own `-- budget: NAME=N ...` line sets its
                      budgets where this does not
    -e SOURCE         the script itself, in place of a file (neither: stdin is the script)
    NAME=VALUE        a value the script reads with arg("NAME", default)
    --help            this, where the docs are, and the mounts in force (alone)
    --version         the mode this `shale` was built in (alone)
  
## The flags the CLI reads (cli.zig parse, script_runner.zig main)
  --args-stdin --budget --check --help --reap --root --undo-on-stop --verbose --version -e -h
## The environment the CLI reads
  HOME SHALE_MOUNTS SHALE_NOW SHALE_PRELUDE SHALE_ROOT

## cli's refusal texts (24)
  --args-stdin: line {d} is not NAME=VALUE
  --args-stdin: line {d}: `{s}` is not a name
  --args-stdin: line {d}: {s} is given twice
  --args-stdin: stdin is the values of a FILE, and there is no FILE
  --budget {s}: a budget is at least 1
  --budget {s}: it is NAME=N
  --budget {s}: no budget is called {s}
  --budget {s}: {s} is at most {d}
  --budget {s}: {s} is not a number
  `-- budget:` names no budget
  `-- budget:` {s}: a budget is at least 1
  `-- budget:` {s}: it is NAME=N
  `-- budget:` {s}: no budget is called {s}
  `-- budget:` {s}: {s} is at most {d}
  `-- budget:` {s}: {s} is not a number
  a `-- budget:` line after the script's first line of code is never read: put it among the comments opening the script
  a second `-- budget:` line: one line says them all
  more than {d} values
  one script: a file or -e, not both
  one script: {s} is a second
  {s} is not an option
  {s} needs a value
  {s}: a value needs a name
  {s}={s} before the script: the script first, then NAME=VALUE

## The time line's rule (shale_host_linux.zig Time)
      pub fn worthSaying(t: Time, verbose: bool) bool {
          return (verbose and (t.runs > 0 or t.waits > 0 or t.sleep_ms > 0)) or t.run_ms + t.wait_ms + t.sleep_ms >= 1000;
      }
      pub fn print(t: Time, w: *std.Io.Writer) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
          try w.print("── time: {d} program{s}, ", .{ t.runs, if (t.runs == 1) "" else "s" });
          try seconds(w, t.run_ms);
          try w.writeAll(" in all");
          const whole = t.run_ms + t.wait_ms + t.sleep_ms;
          for (t.top[0..t.top_len], 0..) |p, i| {
              try w.writeAll(if (i == 0) "; the slowest " else "; ");
              try seconds(w, p.ms);
              try w.print(" ({d}%): {s}", .{ if (whole == 0) 0 else p.ms * 100 / whole, p.argv });
          }
          if (t.waits > 0) {
              try w.print("; {d} job wait{s}, ", .{ t.waits, if (t.waits == 1) "" else "s" });
              try seconds(w, t.wait_ms);
          }
          if (t.sleep_ms > 0) {
              try w.writeAll("; slept ");
              try seconds(w, t.sleep_ms);
          }
          try w.writeAll("\n");
      }
      fn seconds(w: *std.Io.Writer, ms: u64) std.Io.Writer.Error!void {
          try w.print("{d}.{d} s", .{ ms / 1000, ms % 1000 / 100 });
      }
      fn keepEnds(alloc: std.mem.Allocator, argv: []const u8) ![]u8 {
          if (argv.len <= argv_most) return alloc.dupe(u8, argv);
          const room = argv_most - elided.len;
          var head: usize = room / 2;
          while (head > 0 and argv[head] & 0xC0 == 0x80) head -= 1;
          var tail: usize = argv.len - (room - room / 2);
          while (tail < argv.len and argv[tail] & 0xC0 == 0x80) tail += 1;
          return std.mem.concat(alloc, u8, &.{ argv[0..head], elided, argv[tail..] });
      }
      const top_most = 3;
      const argv_most = 80;
      const elided = "…";

## The mounts file (shale_host_setup.zig parseMounts, loadMounts)
  the file unless SHALE_MOUNTS: {s}/.config/shale/mounts

## The gate (tools/shale_gate.zig): its forms, its refusals and its messages
  forms: a launch, `shale [--verbose] [--undo-on-stop] [FILE [--args-stdin]] [NAME=VALUE]... <<'TAG'` (after `cd DIR && ` if wanted; the script on stdin, the last line `TAG`), or the escape, a first line `# want: <tag>: <text>` or `# out-of-scope: <tag>: <text>` (Shale's docs: README.md, then docs/SHALE-AGENTS.md, in the shale repo, ~/showell_repos/shale on this box; its docs and this box's mounts: `shale --help`)
  fn refuse(comptime fmt: []const u8, args: anytype) Verdict {
      return .{ .refused = std.fmt.bufPrint(&why_buf, "shale-gate: " ++ fmt ++ "only " ++ forms, args) catch "shale-gate: refused: only " ++ forms };
  }
  `--budget` takes `NAME=N`; 
  `cd {s}` is not a plain folder; 
  `{s}` is not `shale`; 
  `{s}` is not a plain word; 
  `{s}` is not an option the gate passes; 
  `{s}`: a heredoc is `<<'TAG'`, quoted, the TAG `[A-Z_]+`; 
  a heredoc of more than {d} lines; 
  a launch is one line, or a heredoc's; 
  an escape is `# want: <tag>: <text>` or `# out-of-scope: <tag>: <text>`, the tag `[a-z0-9-]`; 
  no `shale`; 
  shale-gate: no HOME, so the escape cannot be logged: refused
  shale-gate: the escape could not be logged to ~/.local/state/shale/wants.tsv: refused
  shale-gate: the hook's input could not be read: refused
  shale-gate: the hook's input is not the JSON it expects (tool_name, tool_input.command): refused
  the heredoc has no last line `{s}`; 
  the heredoc meets `{s}` twice: a line before its end would close it; 
  too many words; 
  not a plain word: '\'', '"', '$', '`', ';', '|', '&', '<', '>', '(', ')', '*', '?', '\\', '\t', '\r' => return false,

## BY HAND: what the source does not give mechanically
#
# This section is tools/surface_by_hand.txt, copied in whole. Each item is
# a part of the surface that tools/surface.shale cannot read from the code,
# so it is said here, with where the code holds it. An item moves out of
# this list once the tool learns to read it.

### Argument forms the arity column does not show
  edit(p, old, new[, {all, word}]) and edit(p, {{old, new[, all][, word]}, ...}), at most 64 edits a call; the option column lists both forms' keys (builtins_change.zig)
  sort(l[, "asc" | "desc"]), sort(rows, key[, order]), sort(rows, {k1, ...}[, order]), each key a name or {key = name, desc = true}, at most 8 keys (builtins_lists.zig)
  read(p[, offset[, n]]), read_lines(p[, offset[, n]]), count_lines(p[, offset[, n]]), count_in(p, s[, offset[, n]]), find_in(p, s[, offset[, n]]): offsets 0-based
  re_find's `from` is re_find's alone: re_match, re_replace and re_find_all share its option reader, which passes `from` only for re_find (builtins_regex.zig optionsArg), so the option column overstates them
  min(a, b[, c[, d]]), max: two to four integers; path(a[, b[, c[, d]]]): one to four parts
  print(...) takes any number of scalars; tostring and print write nil, true, false, the integer, the string (builtins.zig scalarText)
  host(name, ...) is the core's one door; the Linux host's names are listed above, and metal's host has none (class `host`, "`{s}`: not on this host")
  attempt(f, ...) is the language's, never a builtin: f is a script function declared above; it gives {ok, value} or {ok = false, error, class, line, column, in_function, trail}
  use("mount:path.shale") is a top-level statement with one string literal (parse.zig)
  glob(pattern[, {hidden}]) checks its own key by hand, not through opts_only, so its options show as "-"; the same for any prelude function that reads opts without opts_only or git_opts

### What a value prints as, and what a builtin gives back
  The shapes builtins return (stat's {size, kind, modified}, walk's {path, size, kind, modified} and its {kind = "more"} entry, re_find's {at, text[, groups, group]}, read_lines' {lines, next, done}, run's {argv, code, ended, ms, cpu_ms, out, ...}, job_wait's {ended[, code | signal]}, procs' {pid, ppid, uid, name, args, start}, the tree readers' nodes) are in docs/SHALE.md and docs/SHALE-AGENTS.md, not read here
  table(rows, columns): two spaces between columns, a column of integers aligned right, no newline at the end (builtins_format.zig)
  human(bytes): one decimal, rounded half up, B to EiB; date(seconds): 2026-10-14T03:00:00Z (builtins_format.zig, builtins_time.zig)
  The order of a map's keys is the order first set, and every walk of a map keeps it

### The store's own texts
  A `store` stop's text ends with the store's error, named by zig-webbox's `store` (`FileNotFound`, ...): those names are zig-webbox's, outside this repo, and differ between Linux and metal (builtins_store.zig errorName)
  The store's limits on a name, a path's length and its depth are zig-webbox's (`is_name`'s rule: 1 to 96 bytes of printable ASCII, none of "*/:<>?\|, not . or .., not ending in . or a space)

### Steps and costs
  Every builtin's charge (a step a byte or item, a step for 16 bytes of bulk work, a sort's bound before it runs, a search's stops and compares) is the count `budget()` and `── used:` show, so it is observable; it is held by src/script/charge_test.zig, not by a table here
  The arena's byte counts (`budget().arena_bytes`, where `budget arena` stops) are value.Budgeted's accounting: docs/C-SEAMS.md, "Fidelity"

### The CLI
  Exit codes: 0 the script finished, 1 it stopped (a check's stop too), 2 the run could not begin: the command line, the script's file, stdin, the mounts, a prelude, a `-- budget:` line, SHALE_NOW (script_runner.zig main's `return 2`s)
  stdout carries the script's output and an edit's summary line; stderr carries the header's budgets line, the report, `── time:`, the jobs' lines and the undo's lines, in that order (script_runner.zig main)
  A refusal of the command line prints "shale: <why>" and then the usage
  The script's name in a stop: its FILE as given, "-e", or "stdin" (cli.zig scriptName); a line in a prelude is that prelude's name, a library's its path, the core prelude's "the prelude" (cli.zig placeOf)
  `--help` prints the usage, the docs' paths and the mounts (a secrets mount's folder never shown); `--version` prints "shale <mode>" (script_runner.zig help)
  `NAME=VALUE`s a script never reads with `arg` stop the run before it starts (parse.zig unreadArgStop), unless a name is made as the script runs
  The header's `-- budget:` line: among the opening comments, at most one, the command line's `--budget` winning (cli.zig headerBudgets)
  `--undo-on-stop` keeps at most 64 MiB of prior state (shale_host_linux.zig)
  `call_depth` is settable by `--budget` though the usage text does not list it (cli.zig settable against usage): a drift to settle, not to port silently

### The mounts file
  One `name = value` a line; `#` comments and blank lines passed by; the value an absolute path or `~/...`; then any of ro, tools, secrets, each once, secrets and tools not both, secrets implying read-only (shale_host_setup.zig parseMounts)
  A mount's own path is resolved once, at load; below it no symbolic link is followed (shale_host_linux.zig refuseLinks)
  A missing default file is no mounts; a missing SHALE_MOUNTS file is an error naming it

### The gate
  It passes `[cd DIR && ]shale` or an absolute path ending /shale, then --verbose, --undo-on-stop, --args-stdin, --help, --version, --budget NAME=N and plain words, optionally a `<<'TAG'` heredoc (TAG [A-Z_]+) whose last line is TAG and no earlier line is
  Or the escape: a first line `# want: <tag>: <text>` or `# out-of-scope: <tag>: <text>`, tag [a-z0-9-]+, logged to ~/.local/state/shale/wants.tsv as date, session, kind, tag, text and the command's first 160 bytes, tabs and newlines escaped (tools/shale_gate.zig)

### The browser and the route
  The wasm build's exports (src/shale_wasm.zig) and the signed route's envelope (src/script_route.zig's header) are surfaces of their own, listed here only by name: the route's refusal texts are above, its statuses (400, 403, 409, 500, 501, 503) are in docs/SHALE.md

  builtins 77, host calls 22, prelude functions 93
  stop texts 593, refusal texts 66, budgets 16 (15 a stop names), flags 11
